caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000013
attempts.entry_title: Low-noise encoding of active touch by layer 4 (Hires et al. 2015)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's central findings on layer 4 held in this data, two did not, and two could not be settled. Cells in the C2 barrel fired about one spike per touch at 8 ms latency, with Fano factors near the binomial limit. Layer 4 cells outside C2 responded more weakly to touch, and layer 5 cells fired faster. Decoding of time since touch was less precise than reported (1.1 to 1.4 ms against 0.55 ms), and whisking-phase decoding did not reach the reported resolution. The share of spikes coupled to touch and the 15-neuron touch detection stayed undecided because the paper leaves out cutoff and decoder details, and some behavior and mouse-count claims differed (23 subjects, not 21).
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Hires, Gutnisky, Yu, O'Connor and Svoboda (2015) on dandiset 000013, which holds the 52 loose-seal recordings of the paper (31 L4 cells in C2, 10 L4 cells outside C2, 11 L5 cells) with millisecond whisker tracking during pole localization. It covers the behaviour, the example cell, Table 1, the touch and phase coupled spikes of Figure 3, the population decoders of Figure 4, the modulation indices of Figure 5 and the Fano factors of Figure 6.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hires et al. (2015) from dandiset 000013

outcomes.notes: The electrode location of each file gives 31 L4 C2, 10 L4 surround and 11 L5 C2 cells, one per file, with 115.0 +- 60.6 trials per neuron. The files mark no subset of trials as analysed, so readings (a) and (b) of the trial count are the same.

52 recordings, but 23 subject identifiers. By genotype, C57BL6 9 mice and 22 neurons (paper 7 and 21), Ai32 x PV-Cre 3 mice and 7 neurons (paper 3 and 8), PV-Cre 8 mice and 17 neurons (as the paper), and 3 mice and 6 neurons with a blank genotype, which match the paper's VGAT-ChR2 counts but carry no label.
Hits and correct rejections over all trials, 0.741 +- 0.085 over 52 sessions. The files mark no trials as analysed, so readings (a) and (b) are the same.

Under reading (a), all trials pooled, the pole is in reach for 2.394 s on average, 1.543 to 4.049 s. Under reading (b), session means, the mean is 2.403 s but the range 1.930 to 3.125 s is outside tolerance. 617 of 5978 trials are cut by the end of the recording.
deviations: The sample epoch is read from the `pole_available` series, cut at the end of each 4.5 to 5 s recording; the paper's own measure may extend past it.

outcomes.notes: Measured values are for peak-to-peak as twice the Hilbert amplitude with touch not breaking bouts. Amplitude 15.74 deg and frequency 15.76 Hz match; the mean bout duration is 91.6 ms (69.7 ms when touch breaks bouts) against 261 +- 26.1 ms, so no reading puts all three in tolerance, which the criterion requires; it gives no rule for a partial match. Bouts holding a complete cycle (a variant outside the claims file) last 213.8 to 238.3 ms but then have amplitudes of 33.9 to 35.7 deg. Partially reproduced before the first verification round.

Touches before the response are 3.00 under reading (a) and 3.51 under (b), outside 2.33 +- 0.233 under both. The reaction time is 190 +- 700 ms over 3093 trials, within the tolerance of 234 ms only because the tolerance is the paper's s.d.; 544 trials have the first lick before the first touch, and with those left out it is 420 +- 411 ms. Partially reproduced before the first verification round.

Cell 23 (jf35892, 2010-02-19) is the only L4 C2 cell within tolerance on all three, with rank-sum p = 1.36e-7 over 121 trials. Its rates from pooled spikes and time are 0.727 and 1.909 spikes/s, 2.63-fold, the paper's 0.73, 1.91 and 2.6. Cell 17 has no trial with 500 ms before the pole comes into reach and was not evaluated.
Reading (a), cell 23, gives 7.51, and reading (c), the mean over 52 cells, 7.89; both match. Reading (b), the mean over 41 L4 cells, gives 6.31.

Measured values are for the uniform shuffle, the onset before, 100 ms and the transition cutoff. For cell 23 the window runs from 8 ms to 36 to 38 ms under all 8 readings of the transition cutoff, within tolerance. The spike fraction is 78.4 to 79.1% with the closest onset on either side and 83.6 to 84.6% with the onset before; the time fraction is 19.0 to 20.2% under every reading, against 15.3 +- 1.53%, so no reading meets the criterion (as fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2, all values within tolerance). Partially reproduced before the first verification round.

Cell 23 matches under no reading; its mean 10 ms count before touch is 0.000 to 0.008 against about 0.03, its peak mean count 0.15 to 1.36 and its FF at the peak 0.61 to 1.82. With pooled touches no L4 C2 cell matches (62 units); with grouped touches cell 11 matches in 2 of 394 cell and group units (groups of 20 touches, mean counts 0.0305 and 0.0280 before touch and 0.65 and 0.70 at the peak, FF 0.99 and 1.00 before and 0.37 and 0.32 at the peak). The criterion lets another cell decide the claim, and the two readings of the touches then give different outcomes. With about 400 units tried under the grouped reading, a match in two may come by chance.
deviations: The pre-touch windows are those ending at or before onset (starts -50 to -10 ms), a choice the claims file does not fix; the example cell's pre-touch rate is far from the paper's under any window.

outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), the example cell, 1.474 to 1.505 spikes per first touch, 0.302 to 0.307 per later touch and an 8 ms latency under all 8 window readings of the transition cutoff (9 ms from the all-touch PCTH, also within tolerance). Readings (b) and (c) do not match (means 1.16 to 1.28 and 0.62 to 0.69, medians 0.70 to 0.73 and 0.31 to 0.33). The answer on the cutoff leaves the outcome as it was, since the example cell's window is the same under both starts; it moves the population values of (b) and (c), which were 0.53 to 1.28 and 0.28 to 0.68 over both starts.

Whisking leaves out licking cycles and the 70 ms after each touch, as the claims file defines it. No reading puts both rates in tolerance. The example cell's non-whisking rate is 0.227 spikes/s; its whisking rate 0.777 (2.195 with touch epochs), against 0.67 +- 0.067. The L4 C2 means (1.462 or 3.698), medians (0.376 or 2.270) and pooled rates (1.475 or 3.436) are further off. Without the exclusions (the earlier run's mask, a variant) the example cell's whisking rate is 1.257.

Depth 1.000 from 14 spikes in the phase-analysis cycles counted in exploration time, the criterion's exploration periods, with no spikes in the five bins centred from -75 to 45 deg, around phase 0. Over the same cycles in the whole trial, as Table 1, the depth is also 1.000, from 92 spikes, with one spike in those five bins (0.19 spikes/s at -15 deg).

Measured values are for the first reading of each open detail (uniform shuffle, onset before, 100 ms, transition cutoff, phase window +-t_w, latency from first touches, whisking outside touch epochs). Under the transition cutoff, the criterion's after the answer, 15 of 18 values are within tolerance in all 64 combinations of the other readings, at the threshold for reproduced. The three outside are medians, spikes per first touch (0.70 to 0.73 against 0.87), modulation depth (0.859 against 0.70) and whisking rate (0.376 against 0.33); 12 of the 27 cells with a phase fit have depth 1, and with only the 11 cells of at least 20 phase spikes (a variant) the depth median is 0.444. Whisking periods are read as the claims file defines them, outside touch epochs and leaving out licking cycles and the 70 ms after touch; with touch epochs in, a variant, the count is also 15. Modulation depth uses every phase-analysis cycle of the trial. What the answer changed, the earlier run was blocked because the literal cutoff gave 9 to 14 values and the transition one 14 or 15; the literal cutoff is now a variant only (10 to 14). The 100 and 200 ms curves give 15 alike.

Under the transition cutoff, the criterion's after the answer, 7 to 9 of 17 values are within tolerance, 52 of the 64 combinations of readings below the threshold of 9 (not reproduced) and 12 at it (partially); the readings of the touch window decide which. The medians of spikes per touch, counted among the 17, are never 0; the means of spikes per touch (0.31 and 0.15 under the first reading, against 0.08 and 0.02), the touch-evoked fraction (26.2%, median 23.8%, against 9.2% and 3.6%), the median depth (0.548 against 0.61), the median whisking rate (1.464 against 1.31) and the latency mean (8.1 ms against 18.5) are outside tolerance. Rates, mean depth and minimum ISI match. The literal cutoff, a variant, gives 10 to 11 (partially); the outcome stays blocked because the transition cutoff's own readings straddle the threshold.

Measured values are for the first reading of each open detail, as for table1-l4-c2. Under the transition cutoff 11 to 13 of 18 values are within tolerance in every combination of readings, partially reproduced throughout. Rates (median whisking rate 12.82 against 13.5), mean depth (0.182), the means of spikes per touch and the touch-evoked fraction match; the medians of spikes per first and later touch (0.23 and 0.19 against 0.98 and 0.42), the median depth (0.106 against 0.13), the median latency (4 against 8 ms) and the median minimum ISI (1.5 against 2.7 ms) do not. The literal cutoff, a variant, gives 8 to 11.
All 31 L4 C2 cells have a latency under both readings; of the 10 L4 cells outside C2, 7 have one from first touches and 10 from all touches, not 4. L5, not judged, has 10 or 9.

Reading (a), spikes per touch, gives p < 0.05 for first and later touches with the C2 median higher in all 16 window readings of the transition cutoff (p = 1.0e-4 to 0.0043 and 2.0e-4 to 0.015), and in the 16 of the literal variant. Reading (b), the peak touch rate, gives 148.1 against 25.0 spikes/s (p = 1.63e-5) and 51.3 against 5.6 (p = 1.07e-5). The answer on the cutoff leaves the outcome as it was, as both starts gave it.

L5 medians 12.90 (non-whisking) and 12.82 or 11.52 (whisking, without or with touch epochs) spikes/s against 0.32 and 0.38 or 2.27 in L4 C2 and 1.09 and 1.46 or 1.54 in L4 outside C2; all four rank-sum tests p < 0.05 under both readings (largest 0.0092). Diversity is not judged.

Rank-sum p = 0.584 between L4 C2 (27 cells with a fit, median 0.859) and L4 outside C2 (10 cells, median 0.548), depth from every phase-analysis cycle of the trial. Four L4 C2 cells have no phase-analysis spikes and no depth. With cells of at least 20 phase spikes only (a variant, 11 and 8 cells) p = 0.934; with the cycles counted only in exploration time (the earlier run's, a variant) p = 0.798.

L4 C2 against L5 p = 8.05e-5 and L4 outside against L5 p = 0.0092, L4 medians higher (0.859 and 0.548 against 0.106). With cells of at least 20 phase spikes only (a variant) p = 0.0043 and 0.032; with the cycles counted only in exploration time p = 2.9e-4 and 0.0031.

Whisking leaves out licking cycles and the 70 ms after each touch, as the claims file defines it. With touch epochs left out of whisking neither group changes, L4 C2 p = 0.595 (18 of 31 cells higher, median difference +0.074 spikes/s) and L4 outside C2 p = 0.625, reproduced; with touch epochs in, L4 C2 changes (p = 1.28e-7, 29 of 31 higher, +1.18 spikes/s) and L4 outside C2 does not (p = 0.695), partially reproduced. The criterion's two readings give different outcomes. Without the exclusions (the earlier run's mask, a variant) L4 C2 changes under both readings (p = 5.0e-5 and 2.8e-9); the earlier run recorded partially reproduced.

Signed-rank p = 0.0186 without touch epochs and 0.0322 with them, 9 of 11 cells higher when whisking under each, median of the per-cell differences +2.10 and +2.43 spikes/s, positive under both readings, with whisking leaving out licking cycles and the 70 ms after touch. The group medians are 12.8 and 11.5 spikes/s against 12.9, shown only for comparison. Without the exclusions (a variant) p = 0.0244 and 0.0137. What the answer changed, the criterion now names the median of the per-cell differences as the measure of the increase; the earlier run read it as the group medians and recorded partially reproduced.

Under the transition cutoff, the criterion's after the answer, 66.9 to 75.8% of spikes in 14.6 to 17.6% of exploration time. All 4 readings with the 100 ms curve put both values in tolerance, but only 1 of 4 with the 200 ms curve (the other three cover 16.5 to 17.6% of time), so the readings of the curve's range disagree. What the answers changed, the start of the search is now fixed, and the literal cutoff (38.6 to 64.5% in 8.5 to 13.4%, none within tolerance) is a variant only; the range of the curve, which the paper does not give, is now the criterion's open detail (4), and it alone keeps the claim blocked.

Blocked as it depends on fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2. Every one of its 16 readings with the transition cutoff is outside tolerance on the time fraction (18.8 to 31.7% of spikes in 17.5 to 26.3% of time, against 8.4 +- 13.3% in 3.5%), with the rank-sum test against L4 C2 at p < 0.001. Per cell, under the first reading, five cells (34, 36, 37, 39, 40) have windows of 51 to 86 ms covering 23 to 49% of exploration time; three of them have latencies of 1 to 5 ms. With the answer the literal cutoff (1.5 to 7.4% in 1.2 to 2.6%) is a variant only.

Depends on fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2. Under the transition cutoff 4 of the 8 window readings meet the criterion under both latency readings (2 with the 100 ms curve, 2 with the 200 ms one; 20.8 to 30.6% in 15.4 to 22.5% of time over the 8). With the answer the literal cutoff (5.1 to 14.1% in 3.2 to 8.2%, none) is a variant only; the transition cutoff's readings still disagree.

Depends on fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2. Under the transition cutoff, which the answer makes the rule for t_w too, 74.9 to 81.4% in 22.5 to 28.5% of time, and 1 of 16 readings meets both tolerances (circular shuffle, onset before, 100 ms curve, total width, 76.4% in 22.5%). The preferred phase now comes from the fit over every phase-analysis cycle of the trial; with the sample-epoch fit of the earlier run 4 of 16 met it. The literal cutoff (41.9 to 67.5% in 10.3 to 17.7%, none) is a variant only.

Depends on fig3d-touch-phase-l4c2. None of the 32 readings with the transition cutoff meets the criterion; the fraction is 42.4 to 65.1% (within tolerance) but the time fraction 28.0 to 42.8% against 16.9 +- 1.69%, with the rank-sum test against L4 C2 at p = 9.0e-5 to 0.0029. None of the literal variant meets it.

Depends on fig3d-touch-phase-l4c2. 12 of the 32 readings with the transition cutoff meet the criterion, 6 under each latency reading (all 4 with the 100 ms curve and the total-width phase window, 1 with 100 ms and +-t_w, 1 with 200 ms and the total width); over the 32 the fraction is 32.9 to 48.9% in 23.6 to 36.4% of time. None of the literal variant does.

Blocked as it depends on fig3d-touch-phase-l4c2. Its own criterion holds in all 16 readings with the transition cutoff under both latency readings (L4 C2 4.9 to 10.2%, outside 18.6 to 37.1%, L5 8.3 to 21.4%, outside the largest), and in all 16 of the literal variant. With the sample-epoch phase fit of the earlier run it held in 11 of 16.

With 50 repetitions per population size, the population reaching 95% is 14 (fraction detected) or 12 (percent correct) neurons with exploration non-touch windows; 19, 25 and 25 with percent correct and the pre-touch windows (a1), (a2) and (a3); 19, 30 and 25 with the fraction detected and the same windows. Only 14 is within 15 +- 1.5, so the readings disagree. The fraction detected is now the hit rate at the time point of best percent correct, with ties between thresholds broken at the middle one; the earlier run took the highest hit rate over time points, which with ties broken at the lowest threshold counted every sample as a touch and gave 1 to 4 neurons. Breaking ties at the lowest threshold, a variant, changes only the (a2) fraction-detected value (25). One neuron gives 0.618 to 0.642 percent correct. On synthetic neurons whose touch and non-touch counts come from one distribution, one neuron gives a fraction detected of 0.329 at percent correct 0.541 under either tie rule, against 0.987 under the earlier run's rule.
deviations: Reading (1b) leaves out windows within 60 ms before or 100 ms after a touch onset, a standard choice.
Ties between thresholds of equal training percent correct are broken at the middle one, a choice the claims file does not fix; the lowest one is shown as a variant.

outcomes.notes: Blocked as it depends on fig4a-touch-detection-c2. Its own criterion now holds under every reading. 15 outside neurons reach 0.522 to 0.541 percent correct (upper bound 0.557 to 0.583) and detect 0.196 to 0.351 of touches (upper bound 0.455 to 0.481), against 0.897 to 0.969 in C2, and no outside population up to 200 reaches C2's level at 15. The earlier run's fraction detected (0.91 to 0.94, upper bound 1.000) came from the threshold rule corrected in fig4a-touch-detection-c2.

With add-one smoothing the smallest uncertainty 5 to 15 ms after onset, at 8 ms, is an RMS error of 1.09 to 1.40 ms, a 95% half width of 2.0 ms or 1.96 x RMS of 2.14 to 2.74 ms, under both splits and both sets of time classes (c-all, from -21 ms, and c-post, from 0 ms); none is within 0.55 +- 0.055 ms. The smaller pseudocount (0.01), a variant, gives 1.18 to 1.48 ms RMS. The error falls with population size (19.9 ms at 10 neurons, 1.55 ms at 200). What the answer changed, the time classes and the smoothing are now readings of the criterion; both sets of classes were run before, and the outcome is as before.
deviations: The smaller pseudocount of the variant, 0.01, is a value of our choosing; the criterion gives none.

outcomes.notes: Measured values are from Poisson rates with add-one smoothing and random shifts, the first reading that reaches 76% correct (held-out counts never do). On the phase-tuning cycles of the whole trial (median 494 per C2 cell, 0.107 spikes per cycle, 4 of 31 C2 cells with none), held-out cycle counts with add-one smoothing never reach 76% correct in either group. Poisson rates with add-one smoothing reach it in C2 in only 42 and 38 of the 100 runs (random or even shifts), at a median of 102.8 and 98.2 deg over those runs, so in most runs C2 never reaches it; outside C2 reaches it at 90.0 deg (91 and 89 runs). With a floor rate C2 reaches it at 72.0 or 66.0 deg (91 runs each) and outside C2 at 41.2 or 36.0 deg (100 runs). Under every reading C2 is far from 24 +- 2.4 deg and worse than outside, so all readings give the same failing result; the criterion's "else methods_underspecified" is read as its rule for readings that disagree, which they no longer do. With the cycles restricted to the sample epoch, as the earlier run did and the criterion does not, the floor rate put C2 at 12 to 15 deg and the claim was blocked; that restriction, now a variant, gives 60.0 deg in C2 and 47.1 outside with add-one smoothing.
deviations: The floor rate, one spike over all of a cell's training cycles and bins, is a value of our choosing, as the paper gives none. Cells without a phase fit take preferred phase 0. Tests use 50 samples per phase and phase differences in 6 deg steps.

outcomes.notes: Measured values are for the uniform shuffle, onset before, 100 ms, transition cutoff, order by ranks, velocity at onset and curvature over the touch. Under every reading with the transition cutoff the means are within tolerance, order 0.666 to 0.692, velocity 0.703 to 0.735 and curvature 0.664 to 0.698. The answer on the cutoff leaves the outcome as it was; the earlier measured values (0.853, 0.857, 0.827) came from the literal cutoff, now a variant (0.744 to 0.894, also within tolerance).

Under reading (a), with the transition cutoff, r is 0.618 to 0.788 (velocity, curvature), 0.706 to 0.788 (order, velocity) and 0.588 to 0.641 (order, curvature), and the criterion holds in 16 of 64 combinations of the fig5c readings; under reading (b) it never holds (r 0.27 to 0.51 for velocity and curvature). With the answer the literal cutoff (8 of 64 under (a)) is a variant only; the fig5c readings still give different outcomes.
28 of 31 cells (0.90) under all four readings; 28 or 29 cells have a group and 8 have all five, as most cells have fewer than 100 touches after the 250 ms interval.
deviations: Pre-touch velocity is taken as the frame before onset, fig5c's "pretouch" reading; the claims file does not repeat which reading applies here.

outcomes.notes: Mean minimum FF 0.504 to 0.676 and fraction of units close to the binomial limit 0.79 to 1.00 under all 16 combinations.

With the rate compensated as the answer says (the free rate of Berry and Meister), the model's mean count is 1.001 to 1.034 of the data's, and its FF at the data minimum 0.71 to 0.79. Under reading (2a) the data FF (0.75 to 0.82) is never below the model's by more than the sum of the s.e.m.; under (2b) it is below in 4 of 6 touch readings (61 of 89, 61 of 100, 59 of 99 units and 22 of 31 pooled cells counted from onsets, p = 0.0003 to 0.035) but not with groups of N points from offsets (52 of 91, p = 0.10) or pooled touches from offsets (17 of 31, p = 0.36). What the answer changed, the uncompensated model, now a variant, has a mean count 0.80 to 0.89 of the data's and a higher FF, and gives (2b) in all 6 readings; compensation lowers the model's FF and removes two of them. The outcome is blocked as before.
deviations: The PSTH used for the free rate starts 10 ms before onset so that the integral over the preceding 2.3 ms is defined at the first window.

outcomes.notes: 6.58 +- 5.40 over the 31 L4 C2 cells.
1.56 +- 0.47 within the sample epoch, 1.59 +- 0.47 anywhere in the trial.
1.39 +- 0.60 over all touches, 1.34 and 1.36 +- 0.74 over touches after a 250 ms interval.
0.85 and 0.86 over all touches, 0.70 to 0.74 over touches after a 250 ms interval, under both readings of the window starts.
0.504 to 0.691 under all 16 readings, with the five conditions in the paper's order under each.

0.107 (L4 C2) and 0.121 (all L4) spikes per cycle as means over cells, 0.116 and 0.124 pooled, over the phase-analysis cycles of the whole trial (17669 and 27769 cycles); 11 cells are above 0.15. Inside the sample epoch only, the earlier run's cycles and a variant here, 0.092 to 0.114.

findings.statement: In 36 files the SpikeTrain timestamps run 10 ms before the CurrentClampSeries timestamps of the same samples (the spike samples line up with the voltage one for one); in 16 files they agree. Under the spike timestamps the median L4 C2 touch-response peak is 8 ms in the files without the offset and 12 ms in those with it (rank sum p = 0.016); under the voltage timestamps it is 8 and 22 ms. The data are consistent with the voltage timestamps of the 36 files being 10 ms late, and a residual 4 ms difference under the spike timestamps is not explained.
In 38 files the CurrentClampSeries data, with the stated conversion of 0.001 to volts, span only 2 to 26 microvolts, so the conversion is off by 1000; in the other 14 they span 3 to 28 mV.

In 38 files theta_filt, described as theta_at_base filtered 6 to 60 Hz, is not the signal the stored amplitude and phase come from (up to 46 deg apart); in 14 it equals amplitude times cos(phase). The stored amplitude and phase match a 6 to 60 Hz Butterworth band-pass and Hilbert transform of theta_at_base.
set_point is described as the amplitude of the Hilbert transform of theta_at_base but follows theta minus its band-passed part (r 0.96 to 1.00), and holds missing values in 23 files.
pole_position is described in mm, but its values range over several scales between files, 0.2 to 1.6 in some, 992 to 13888 (motor steps) in others, about 1e8 in others, and up to 1.4e12 in one.

Three subjects (anm211295, anm215592, anm217330; six cells) have no genotype, the paper's VGAT-ChR2 mice by their counts. The files hold 23 subjects where the paper reports 21 mice, and the C57BL6 and Ai32 x PV-Cre counts differ from the paper's by one cell each, so the mapping of subjects to the paper's animals is not given.
30 files are named with an ogen suffix, but no file holds an optogenetic stimulus series and stim_present is 0 in every trial.

first_lick_time disagrees with the lick onset series in some trials, by up to 3.1 s; 47 trials have licks in the series and no first_lick_time, and 136 have a first_lick_time and no lick in the series.

The paper's analysis code (touch windows, phase decomposition, decoders, clustering, Fano factors) is not public; the repository it links holds only the contact detection, so several procedures could not be fixed and are asked about.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (verifier-1, run 39625737606; same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The handover of the author-answers run (commit dfd53645), the executed notebook with the conclusions and summary removed, the helper module and the claims file. The verifier also checked the archive's asset list for the blocked claims and read the paper.

disagreements.reason: Mean bout duration is 70 to 92 ms against 261 under all four claimed combinations. Only the non-claim variant of bouts with at least one cycle reaches the duration, and its amplitude then fails.

Touches before the response are 3.00 (reading a) and 3.51 (reading b), against 2.33 +- 0.233. The reaction time of 190 ms passes only because its s.d. is 700. The pooled reaction time includes 544 negative values (lick before first touch); the claim fails on the touch counts regardless (does not affect the conclusion).
Time fraction is 19.0 to 20.2% against 15.3 +- 1.53 in all 8 criterion readings.

Reproduced, weakly. Cell 23 fails, its pre-touch mean count is 0.003 against 0.03. Under reading (b) one cell (cell 11, one touch group) matches out of about 600 cell x group tries, which is what the criterion asks. The verifier also reports, as a question about the claims file, that reading (b) accepts any of about 600 tries, which invites a match by chance, and could not check the row in which cell 11 matches or how many units were tested.

7 to 9 of 17 values under the criterion readings; 52 of 64 combinations fall below 9. Latency is 8.1 against 18.5, and the spikes-per-touch medians are never 0. In the Table 1 cell, the line meant to add the zero-median check does nothing and the check is not added to n_ok, so n_ok counts out of 15 against thresholds set out of 17; this does not change the outcome, because the medians are never 0.

Time fraction is 17.5 to 26.3% against 3.5 +- 0.35 under every criterion reading. The verifier also reports, as a question about the claims file, that the "cross" cutoff rule says nothing about cells with no real rise; for L4 outside and L5 cells noise crossings place long windows, 17 to 26% of exploration time where the paper gives 3.5%, and the literal-start variant gives 1.3 to 2.6%. It asked for per-cell t_on and time fraction for these cells.
Time fraction is 27 to 42% against 16.9 +- 1.69 under every criterion reading.

Provisional. The criterion holds under all four percent-correct readings, 0.53 to 0.55, upper bound below 0.60, near the 50% chance level. It fails under the "detected" readings, which problem 2 invalidates.
Reading (a), 16 of 64 sub-readings match. Reading (b), 0 match. r_vc ranges from 0.62 to 0.79 and is often not the largest.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hires et al. (2015) from dandiset 000013
